title: Who ran it
lede: Roles are from the filings and announcements cited. We have left out people and details we could not source.

people.name: Steve Case
people.role: Chairman and CEO of America Online; chairman of AOL Time Warner
people.text: Led AOL through its growth and agreed the Time Warner merger, becoming chairman of the combined company.[^22] He later recalled the plan in the early years as spending 10% of a subscriber’s lifetime revenue to acquire them.[^24]
people.later: Richard Parsons had succeeded him as chairman by May 2003; Case was still a director in March 2004.[^7]

people.name: Jan Brandt
people.text: Ran the disk and disc mailings. By her account the first large mailing, in 1993, drew a 10% response.[^24][^25]

people.name: Bob Pittman
people.role: President and COO of America Online
people.text: Named co-chief operating officer of AOL Time Warner, with Richard Parsons, when the merger was announced.[^22]

people.name: Gerald Levin
people.role: CEO of Time Warner, then of AOL Time Warner
people.text: Agreed the merger for Time Warner and became chief executive of the combined company.[^22]

people.name: Richard Parsons
people.role: CEO of AOL Time Warner from May 2002; chairman from May 2003
people.text: Was in charge when the company took “AOL” out of its name on October 16, 2003.[^7]

people.name: Tim Armstrong
people.role: Chairman and CEO of AOL Inc.
people.text: Led the independent company and its turn to advertising and media, and stayed to run AOL under Verizon.[^15]
people.later: Became chief executive of Oath when Verizon combined AOL with Yahoo in 2017.[^28]

people.name: Elwood Edwards
people.text: Recorded “Welcome,” “You’ve Got Mail,” “Files done” and “Goodbye” on a cassette deck in his living room in 1989.[^26]
